preamble: The voiced alveolar affricate /dz/ palatalizes to the alveolo-palatal [dʑ] before a high front vowel. In Seneca (Iroquoian), /dz/ before [i] varies freely with [dʑ] (Chafe 1967). It is an allophonic palatalization, not a phonemic merger.

examples.note: Optional palatalization in free variation with [dz] before [i]; among younger speakers /dz/ is reported to be merging with /dʒ/ (spelled j).

sources: Chafe, W. (2015). A Grammar of the Seneca Language. University of California Press. https://doi.org/10.1525/9780520961647
